findings.title: Optimized paginator raises TypeError on the datetime key, so the new mode 500s on the first page
findings.description: `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. For the endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"`, that value is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69), and `math.ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. On the first request the cursor value is 0, so `_build_next_values` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122) calls `key(results[0])` whenever the org has entries. Nothing catches the error, so the endpoint returns 500 for any admin who passes `optimized_pagination=true`. Follow-up pages are also broken: `value_from_cursor` (lines 842-843) returns the raw millisecond integer, whereas `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` (paginator.py:238-241) converts it to a datetime. `build_queryset` (paginator.py:112-126) then binds that integer against a timestamp column, which Postgres will likely reject. The endpoint path is src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73-83, and no test covers it.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch cannot work, and its comments describe access that does not exist
findings.description: `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59). For an admin, a cursor with a negative offset takes the branch at line 877, which passes the negative value straight into a queryset slice. Django does not support negative slice bounds, so this raises instead of paginating. The comments at lines 874-879 say the branch "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" and that "permissions are checked at the queryset level." Neither is true. The queryset is only filtered by `organization_id` (organization_auditlogs.py:48), and permissions are enforced by `OrganizationAuditPermission`. Remove the branch and its comments.

findings.title: Base `BasePaginator.get_result` change alters every paginated endpoint, with a false comment
findings.description: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes the behavior of all paginators. For next-page cursors, a negative offset used to raise and now silently returns the first page. In the equal-value branch of `_build_next_values` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:139-142), the next offset is still computed from the raw negative value, so the following page is also wrong. The comment ("allow negative offsets", "safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is false for both branches. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` does not depend on this change, since it has its own copy of the else-branch at lines 883-886. Revert lines 179-184 to `stop = offset + limit + extra` and `queryset[offset:stop]`.

findings.title: Feature gate uses the raw `is_superuser` flag instead of the active-superuser check
findings.description: `request.user.is_superuser` is the database flag. `is_active_superuser(request)` (src/sentry/auth/superuser.py:143-147) also requires an active superuser session. The same endpoint's permission class uses `is_active_superuser` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124), so this gate is looser than the access check beside it. The gated mode does not expose extra rows, but the comment calls it "for authorized administrators," and reviewers will likely copy the pattern. Other endpoints in the repo do use the raw flag (organization_events.py:463, system_options.py:79), so this is a divergence from the nearby convention rather than a repo-wide violation.

findings.title: `member` is dereferenced without a None check on every request
findings.description: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346). The `or` only short-circuits for superusers. `enable_advanced` is computed before `use_optimized` is checked, so a non-superuser with no membership raises `AttributeError` on every GET, including the default path with no query param. `Access.scopes` returns `scopes_upper_bound` when `member` is None (src/sentry/auth/access.py:435-436), so a non-member principal whose access carries `org:write` could reach this line. I did not trace every token type to confirm that. Compute the value only inside the `use_optimized` branch and guard against None.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates the base paginator and claims optimizations it does not have
findings.description: `get_result` (lines 845-911) reproduces `BasePaginator.get_result` (paginator.py:136-215) almost line for line. `get_item_key` (lines 838-840) is identical to `Paginator.get_item_key` (paginator.py:222-224). The only real difference is the negative-offset branch, which does not work (see above). The class docstring (lines 822-832) promises an "optimized query path," "streamlined boundary condition handling," and "negative offset support," and the code has none of these. Any future fix to the base class would have to be copied here. If the mode is kept, subclass `DateTimePaginator` and drop the copied methods; if not, delete the class.

findings.title: No tests cover the new paginator, the new endpoint branch, or negative offsets
findings.description: The diff adds no tests. The existing file covers default listing and filters (lines 22-199) but not `optimized_pagination=true`, the non-admin fallback, or negative cursor offsets. One admin request against an org with a single audit entry would have exposed the TypeError in the first finding. The existing negative-offset test (tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py:143-153) covers only `OffsetPaginator`, so the change to `BasePaginator` is untested.

findings.title: Cursor comment describes a change that is not in the code
findings.description: The two added comment lines say negative offsets are now allowed "for advanced pagination scenarios" and "enable efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets." The code line `self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged, and `Cursor` already accepted negative integers. Remove the comment, since it misdescribes the code.

findings.title: Formatting issues that a pre-commit or ruff-format run would flag
findings.description: Line 72 is whitespace-only, and line 89 (`order_by="-datetime", `) has a trailing space. In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, lines 818-820 contain three blank lines before `class OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and lines 824, 827, and 829 in the docstring have trailing whitespace.
